result.report:
PASS for the stated partial result: this is an actual counterexample on the specified cyclic triangle squared. The argument establishes P_gamma(u)=gamma, membership in real PAPC and the regularizable domain, and the complete contact integral −8. It does not complete the arbitrary balanced-pair classification.

Both factor graphs retain their bounded cycles, primitive leaves, unit weights and saturated lattice Z². Each junction has rank two and positive relation cone generated by (1,1,1). The 36 product edge cells have saturated direct-sum tangent lattices and balanced unit product weights.

The admissibility checks hold. Gamma is a maximum of 20 rational ambient affine functions, so its restriction has finite rational spatial domains. The obstacle is bounded, continuous, rational-domain PA and nonseparable. Jensen's inequality proves actual PC for every admitted PCC, including arbitrary real centres and remote rational endpoints. The supporting-affine-function argument proves PAPC against every nonnegative real local cycle on every ordinary open; it does not merely test the given top cycle. The recession estimate gives gamma_sigma,lin(v) >= rho(v)/4 > 0 for every nonzero recession vector.

The raw-envelope proof is global and does not require competitor continuity. All nonzero vertices of the chosen gamma structure have rho >= 1 and therefore zero obstacle. The three rational diagonal endpoints in (7) form an admitted PCC with centre (A,A) and cap values zero, forcing every competitor q to satisfy q(A,A) <= gamma(A,A). The supplied homogenization proof correctly establishes vertex-plus-recession generation for every nonempty pointed rational cell. Its far-endpoint PCCs retain arbitrary real barycentric coefficients and give q(x) <= gamma(x)+(T/L)max(C_q,0). Taking L to infinity establishes q <= gamma everywhere. Gamma itself is a competitor, proving exact equality and hence exact two-sided reference growth.

The divisor reconstruction is valid. Tangential changes of normal lifts cancel in (2). The three refinement cases preserve cycle balancing and divisor coefficients, including the second divisor. The saturated-plane index chi correctly makes s/chi a representative of the primitive quotient normal. Formula (3) proves balancing of the first divisor. Commutativity in the two-dimensional scope also follows directly: the mixed vertex coefficient expands as a sum over cones of (omega/chi)(a(s)b(r)+a(r)b(s)), minus sum_r t_r a(r)b(r), which is symmetric in a and b. No external intersection theorem is needed.

At (A,A), all twelve local cones have saturated index one. The complete first divisor has axis weights 2,2,0 in each factor and diagonal weights 2,2,4. The diagonal germ values are zero; the four nonzero axis contributions are each two. Thus the full recursive mass is eight, with the original branching axes and newly introduced diagonal faces retained. The normalization is the recursive intersection normalization, without division by 2!.

The complete integral follows analytically, without requiring the other masses: the PA measure is supported on the finite vertex set, every other original vertex has gap zero, and the gap at (A,A) is −1. Obstacle refinements introduce only inherited coefficients or zero coefficients at new vertices. Constant-shift approximants gamma+1/j decrease uniformly, remain PAPC in the two-sided growth class, and have exactly the same divisors and measures. Thus the already-PA envelope has the asserted operator value, with no additional mass at infinity.

I also independently reconstructed the finite rational domain enumeration and both divisor stages. It agrees with 53 top domains, 12 vertices, masses 8 at AA, BB and CC, masses 4,9,9 at the three diagonal cutoffs, and zero at the six remaining vertices. The cutoff indices include 16; their fractional first-divisor weights were retained. Total mass is 46 and the weighted contact sum is −8. This corroborates the ancillary table; the global envelope proof and complete-integral proof do not rely on numerical diagnostics.

The rectangle-roof supporting diagnostic is correct in its stated coarse reconstruction scope. Its branch slopes arise from the ambient linear form (x−y)/2. The displayed roofs satisfy the corner caps but violate the actual junction PCC by 1/12, establishing the claimed absence of a greatest roof-feasible node assignment. It is not used as a contact counterexample.

I checked the cited definitions and named proof boundaries against the authentic [BMPS v1 PDF, dated 10 March 2026](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.08664v1). Its literal PA convention is correctly distinguished from the explicitly defined real extension. None of its approximation, locality, continuity or intersection theorems is essential to this proof. The trailing supporting-proofs heading contains no additional bodies; that is a harmless presentation issue because no predecessor theorem is imported. Artifact and historical provenance assertions are not theorem premises. No substantial mathematical repair is required.
